# Independent audit of the R4 all-normal certificate

The finite certificate and its geometric interpretation PASS. This certifies the specific product body's depth, not Oertel's conjecture.

Sources audited: `candidate d06bf37b63fb4cbb`, `supporting computation search_r4_exact_bernstein_tetra_slab_recovery.py`, and the complete tree in `supporting computation r4_exact_bernstein_tetra_attempt_slab_recovery.json`.

Independent replay: `supporting computation verify_r4_bernstein_independent_two_sided.py`. Saved output: `supporting computation r4_bernstein_independent_two_sided_checks.txt`.

It checks all 15,099 nodes, 11,188 terminal tetrahedra, 223,497 raw polynomial coefficients (15,767 zero), and exact total relative volume one. It uses direct polynomial multiplication, not the search program's polarization expression. There are no pending or unresolved nodes. No floating-point decision enters the replay.

## 1. Actual normal parameterization

The base is the integer points of the triangle with vertices `(4,0),(0,4),(-4,-4)`. Its vertex permutations are induced by unimodular linear maps and preserve the 31-point set. Permutations of the continuous triangle vertices independently preserve its area measure. Consequently every normal having a nonzero continuous part may be arranged to have base coefficients `a>=0`, `-a/2<=b<=a` and continuous ordered vertex values `h0>=h1>=h2`, summing to zero, with `h0>0`.

The compact chart uses `a+h0=1`, not the unweighted sum of the maximum actual base vertex value and the maximum continuous value: the former is `4a`. This is a wording correction only; the displayed tetrahedron and its complete normal coverage are correct. Set `h0=1-a`, `h1=c`, `h2=-1+a-c`. Its parameter vertices are exactly the four displayed vertices in the interface.

For a triangle, the divided-difference formula for its captured area fraction is the stated signed sum of `(L+h_j)_+^2`; its denominator is positive when the three heights are distinct. This is the captured side `L+h>=0`, not its complement. Summing is over the actual 31 lattice points, without integration in the integer variables.

## 2. Integer homogeneous scaling and lower polynomial

In barycentric coordinates of the compact parameter tetrahedron, the search vectors `f_j` are exactly `2(L+h_j)`. Its vectors `g0,g1,g2` are respectively `2(h1-h2)`, `2(h0-h2)`, and `2(h0-h1)`. They are nonnegative on the entire domain.

Define

    E = g0 sum f0_+^2 - g1 sum f1_+^2 + g2 sum f2_+^2
        - (40/3) g0 g1 g2.

This is eight times the interface polynomial. On a leaf, omit a positive summand whose linear factor changes sign; retain a negative summand as its full square whenever the factor is positive anywhere. The resulting polynomial E_low satisfies E_low<=E pointwise. Positive factors nonnegative everywhere are retained exactly; factors everywhere nonpositive in the negative sum contribute zero. Thus unresolved sign hyperplanes do not invalidate a terminal certificate.

The integer `tot` in the search is nine times the degree-three Bernstein coefficient of E_low, equivalently three times the Bernstein coefficient of `3E_low`. The search's short coefficient comment should specify which polynomial is meant. The sign test is correct.

The independent checker expands `3E_low` directly in monomials of the leaf's four nonnegative barycentric variables and checks every coefficient nonnegative. Each monomial coefficient is a positive multinomial factor times its degree-three Bernstein coefficient, so this independently verifies the same implication.

Vertices are stored as nonnegative primitive integer homogeneous vectors v. The polynomial is evaluated at `sum lambda_i v_i`, whose normalized point is `(sum lambda_i v_i)/(sum lambda_i sum(v_i))`. This parameterizes exactly the same Euclidean tetrahedron as the normalized vertices `v_i/sum(v_i)`. Homogeneity of degree three and positivity of the denominator preserve the asserted sign. There is no omitted vertex denominator.

## 3. Complete exact coverage

Every intersection vertex is checked independently against the normalized Euclidean edge formula. Each child lies on one closed side of the chosen cutting plane. A one-positive cut gives the corner tetrahedron and the three-tetrahedron pulling triangulation of its truncated complement. A two-positive cut gives two triangular prisms, each split into the displayed three tetrahedra. Reversal handles a three-positive cut. These are triangulations with disjoint interiors; zero vertices are their closed limits, with zero-volume children discarded.

For every recorded split the replay additionally verifies the exact sum of child volumes equals the parent volume. It follows recursively that the terminal tetrahedra cover the original tetrahedron. Every path occurs exactly once, every expected child path is present, no extra records remain, and the exact terminal-volume sum is one. The computation has no depth cutoff leaves or unverified boundary pieces.

## 4. Repeated values, pure integer cuts, and actual maximum

For distinct continuous heights, the positive denominator converts the nonnegative polynomial to captured mass at least `(40/3)|K|`. Repeated heights follow by continuity: every nonzero continuous normal has zero area on its boundary in each triangle fiber, and the sum has finitely many fibers.

For a nonzero pure integer normal, approximate by normals with a nonzero continuous component. Pointwise the limiting closed-cap indicator is at least the limsup of the approximating indicators. Reverse Fatou for this finite measure therefore retains the lower bound, including the complete area of any boundary fibers. Any halfspace containing the proposed center contains its through-center translate with the same normal.

The base and continuous vertex-permutation groups preserve the mixed measure. Their orbit average of any point is `(0,g_K)`, an actual mixed point. Ambient depth superlevel sets are convex, so this point has depth at least that of every other point. The canonical caps have twelve full fibers and three centroid triangle caps; hence they attain exactly `12+3(4/9)=40/3` fiber-area units. Therefore the actual maximum normalized depth of this product is exactly `40/93`.

This example is far above the OC target `1/9`. Its role is solely the stated auxiliary efficiency obstruction. The interface's former unproved-status paragraphs can be updated after attaching the finite certificate and replay; they are not themselves proof gaps in the completed certificate.
